column2: How do I add a house to a census?
column3: Open the census (the person’s record → Censuses → ✎). At the bottom, “🏠 House”: choose the house and its period, then “🔗 Link” (it is saved straight away), or “＋ New house” to draw it, already linked. “↗ Open the house” opens it directly at the period of this census.

column2: Where can I see a person’s houses?
column3: On their record, the “🏠 Houses” block: the houses where they are an inhabitant, linked to a room, or in a linked census, with their image, the period and “↗ Open”. It can be arranged like the other blocks (Settings → Appearance → record blocks).

column2: How do I see the house change over the years?
column3: In the house, “🕰 Periods” (at the top): the house you drew becomes the first period (a name, a year or a date), and “＋ New period (copy of this one)” makes a copy at another date (1900, 1936…) that you change: a room added, a wall knocked down, other furniture, another roof. ‹ › or the menu at the top move from one period to another, in 2D as in 3D; “▶” plays them in date order. House tab → “🕰 The periods”: ✎ to rename, change the date or link the period to a census, × to delete it.

column2: How do I link a period of the house to a census?
column3: House tab → “📋 The censuses”: the menu next to each census chooses its period (or ✎ on the period → “Linked to the census”). From the census window, “↗ Open the house” then opens it at that period.

column2: How do I download free, royalty-free 3D furniture?
column3: Furniture → “📦 Online library”: models from Poly Haven, royalty-free (CC0), can be searched and imported in one click. “ZIP pack” tab: download a CC0 pack (Kenney, Quaternius…) from the author’s site, choose the .zip file and tick the models to keep. They arrive in “My objects”, with their licence, author and source (✎ to see them).

column2: How do I hide or arrange the furniture categories and objects?
column3: Furniture → “⚙️ Arrange”: tick what you want to see and arrange the categories with ↑ ↓, then the objects in each category. “↺ Reset to default” goes back to the original order.

column2: How do I make a map to the right scale, without distorting it?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → 🗺️ Map → “＋ New map”: choose the size, then locate the map (the place and the width covered): the scale is then correct. The “Scale grid” (100 m, 1 km… squares, never printed) helps place each thing in its place, and a selected object shows its real length or area.

column2: What are “Coat of arms mode” and “Map mode” at the top of the drawing for?
column3: Tick them to show on the right the coat of arms or map tab and menu; unticked, they stay hidden to keep the editor simple.

column2: How do I grey out (or not) the rows I have unticked in lists to arrange?
column3: Settings → “Menus, column and lists” → Column tab → “👁 Hidden rows in lists to arrange”: “Leave them as they are”, or “Grey them out” with the level of grey you want. It applies to all the lists where you tick what is shown (menus, lists, Reorder, Customise…).

column2: How do I arrange the lists (or the Settings pages) into groups?
column3: At the bottom of the left column, “Reorder”: tick or untick “Arrange in groups”. In groups: arrange, rename, create or delete groups, move a list to another group, choose whether groups are open or closed. As a single list: arrange with ↑ ↓. Each way keeps its settings, you find them again when switching. “My lists” always stay at the bottom, apart: they can only be arranged among themselves. The same setting is in Settings → “Menus, column and lists” → “Lists” tab (for Lists, “Reorder” takes you straight there).

column2: How do I put a drawing into a group or a layer?
column3: Layers tab: drag the row onto the group (it turns blue); or choose the object then “📁 Put into…”. Double-click on a name to rename it.

column2: How do I arrange or hide the buttons of the House tool, or give it my shortcuts?
column3: In the tool, “⚙️ Customise” (at the top), or Settings → “Editing, retouching, page layout and sound” → “🏠 House (plan and 3D)” editor: top bar, tools in the left column, 3D view bar and panel tabs, to tick and arrange, to keep as named sets; and below, your keyboard shortcuts for each command.

column2: Can “Ask a question” calculate, not just list?
column3: Yes (Research → Ask a question in French). Besides lists (“Which ancestors were bakers in Lille before 1850?”), it answers questions that need a calculation: the relationship between two people (“What is the relationship between Jean Dupont and Marie Durand?” → second cousins, cousin once removed, common ancestors, civil degree); records (who lived longest, died youngest, largest family, married youngest or latest, biggest age gap between spouses, oldest ancestor); averages (age at marriage, at death, at first child, children per couple); the most frequent (first names, surnames, occupations, communes, months and seasons); one person (“When was… born”, “Where did… die”, “How old was… at their marriage”, “How old would… be today”); periods (“Who lived through the Great War?”, “Who was 20 in 1914?”, “Who was alive in 1900?”); counts (“How many ancestors do I have?”, by generation). You can add “men”, “women”, “ancestors”, “in the 19th century”… The list of examples is under the box: “And also questions that need a calculation”. The questions are typed in French.

column2: Does the app recognise faces in photos?
column3: Yes, on your computer only: Lists → Media → “👤 Faces” (this tool brings together the old “Face detection” and “Who is who?”). Step ① Find the faces: choose the photos, then “🔍 Analyse”; the list “Photos with faces to name” opens each photo in the viewer with the faces framed (click on a frame to say who it is). Step ② Who is it?: first identify a few faces by hand, at least once per person; “💡 Suggestions” then says “this is probably Marie Martin” (very likely or likely, with the percentage of likeness): ✓ Yes, Someone else… or Ignore, or accept them all at once for the very likely ones; “👥 Grouped unknowns”: faces that look alike from one photo to another, to name in one go. Each confirmed face becomes an ordinary identification on the photo; “↶ Undo” removes it. The model (≈ 13 MB) is downloaded once, checked by its fingerprint; the photos are not sent anywhere.

column2: How do I read a ten-year index with the app?
column3: Lists → Record indexes (or Research → Archive record index) → “📑 Read a ten-year index”. Five steps: ① the photo of the index (media window), the commune, the period (“1853-1862”) and the kind of records; ② drag the blue lines between the columns (Surname, First names, Date, Kind of record…) or take a known template, then “↧ Find the rows”; ③ the app reads each row on this computer (printed index), or with the handwriting reader if it is installed; otherwise you type it in by hand, with the row’s strip in front of you; ④ you check the grid, with the image alongside (uncertain cells are in yellow, dates without a year take the one from the row before, a date outside the period is flagged); ⑤ the “Ten-year index” record index is created (with “↶ Undo”), then the app suggests the records: 🔗 Link or ＋ Create the record (with the birth or death).

column2: The reading engine does not load: can I still index my table?
column3: Yes. In “📑 Read a ten-year index”, at step ③, “✍ Type the rows by hand”: a quick grid (Enter or ↓ for the next row), with the strip of each row of the image above. The engine (printed text) is downloaded once with the Internet; the handwriting reader is installed in Settings → Handwriting recognition.

column2: How do I find a photo in the database from another one (reverse search)?
column3: “🔍 Search for a similar image”: in the viewer (button under the photo), in the ⋯ or right-click of a thumbnail in Lists → Media, or at the top of Media. Start from a photo in the database, or drop / paste (⌘V) an image from your computer: it is only used for searching, it does not go into the media. The results are sorted: ＝ identical (the same file), ≈ very close (resized, re-saved, retouched, another format), ⬚ cropped / zoomed (a piece of the photo, framed in blue in the preview), ～ similar (same scene, another shot), with the percentage. “See” puts the two images side by side; “🔍 Compare two photos” opens the comparison tool. Everything is calculated on this computer: the app keeps a “fingerprint” of each photo (calculated in the background, in small batches; if you close, it resumes where it left off; a retouched or rotated photo is recalculated by itself).

column2: How do I find duplicate photos, even retouched or cropped?
column3: Lists → Media → “👯 Duplicate images” (it replaces the old “Duplicate search” and also finds duplicate sounds and PDFs). The groups are sorted into Perfect (the same file), Retouched, Cropped / zoomed, Resized and Other format; “Sensitivity” suggests more or less different photos. In each group, the largest is suggested as “★ Kept” (“★ Keep” to choose another), then “👯 Keep ★ and merge”: its links gather those of the others (records, events, labels, albums, collections, investigations, portrait, face areas put back in the right place). The others go “🗑 To the bin” (the file stays on the disk) or “🗂 As versions” of the kept photo. “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before, and the “🗑 Duplicates bin” lets you “↶ Restore” a merge later. “🙈 Not a duplicate” is remembered (“🙈 Not duplicates” to go back on it).

column2: How do I compare two photos to see if it is the same person?
column3: “🔍 Compare two photos”: from the viewer (“🔍 Compare with…”), Lists → Media, a record’s Media block (🔍), or Comparison → Images. The two photos side by side, as a fade (slider) or as a curtain, with the same zoom; “✨ Find the eyes automatically” (face model, on this computer) or “👁 Place the eyes” (two clicks per photo) brings the two faces to the same size; black and white, contrast, notes. The calculated likeness stays cautious: “this is not proof” (age, light, family resemblance…). “💾 Save” keeps the comparison, linked to the two photos and the people: Lists → Editing tools → 🔍 Compare two photos.

column2: How does the 👤 Faces tool work?
column3: Lists → Media → “👤 Faces”. Two tabs: ① Find the faces (the app spots the faces in the chosen photos and calculates their “fingerprint”) and ② Who is it? (it suggests a name based on faces already identified). Start small: the app picks the lightest batch automatically, often “Photos marked with faces” (the person’s photo, a record’s portrait, faces already identified, “portrait” or “face” label). You can also take the photos shown in the Media list (with your search), those of a person, a label, an album or a folder, a period (“between 1900 and 1950”), the N most recent, or all. “Skip photos already analysed” avoids redoing the work.
